subject.scene: wide Home scene (design/home-scene.html, generated from desktop/plugin.js)

floors.how_a_run_fails: a run is under the cap floor when its rendered cap height at that width is below 11 px; it is under the contrast floor when ANY glyph-core pixel behind it is below 3.0:1 (the worst pixel, not the median). WCAG AA for normal text is 4.5:1 and is reported separately, not applied as this card's floor.

type_ladder.note: the smallest runs sit on two adjacent type steps; the floor is not reachable by a token swap alone
type_ladder.scene_steps_in_use: meta 0.875rem = 14 px (card titles, cap 9.24); body 1rem = 16 px (CTA labels, cap 10.56); heading/display are clamp()ed against the route container (1cqi) and land at 32.64 / 64 px at 1344

method.driver: the CP-TEXT-GATE method (tests/fixtures/scene-text/README.md) extended with a cap probe, a floor-raise probe and background sampling; no test or product file is edited. The probe is committed at probes/legibility-2026-11/ (measure.mjs drives Chromium, analyse.py turns the captures into this document); the hashes below are the committed files.
method.cap_height: the run's element keeps its own glyphs transparent while an absolutely positioned single capital H, set in the run's computed font, is painted at the run's own text-rect origin (placement residual <= 0.02 px, verified before every capture). Cap height is the face's cap ratio measured at 200 px times the run's rendered font size, corroborated by the H's pixel span at >=50 % coverage (agreement <= 1 px, the pixel span is the tighter antialias boundary).
method.contrast: the declared colour composited over the pixels of the `without-<n>` capture at the run's ink mask (glyph-core pixels, coverage >= 85 %), WCAG 2.x relative luminance; `min` is the worst pixel behind a glyph
method.widths: two fresh renders of the shipped page at route width 1344 and 1200; at 1200 the scene plate is transform-scaled by 1200/1344, so the same authored type paints smaller (measured scene scale 0.892857)
method.determinism: a second base capture is pixel-identical (0 differing px at both widths); after every probe was removed the page returned to its base paint inside every measured text rect (0 px above the ink threshold), while rotated card/tag edges re-rasterised by up to 35/255 outside the text rects, which is why all masks are restricted to the run's own text rects
